title: Station Bridge ICD (docs/04 9.7, docs/06 5) still shows the 3-field hello and no M line, under a 'VENTUNO Q' heading
description: The code sends 'H|<fw>|<rcu -1/0/1>|<kb>|<rcu age s>' (sketch.ino:1704; frontpanel.parse_hello). The rcu field is the result of the last rcu_mode() call, not 'RCU present'. The GDS also sends 'M|sync|tx|rssi|margin|lost|clock' on fp_line. docs/04:897-901 documents fp_line as S/Q only and the hello as "H|<fw>|<rcu>|<kb>"; docs/06:204 says "H|<fw>|<rcu 0/1>|<kb 0/1>" = 'RCU present'. Both sections still say VENTUNO Q. These files are outside the three named docs but are the interface definition of the station link (the docs phase may still be pending).
failure_scenario: Someone writes a replacement station sketch or a test tool from docs/04. They send a 3-field hello (accepted, but the RCU state stays 'unknown') and do not implement the M line, so the LED matrix stays blank.
proposed_fix: Update docs/04 9.7 and docs/06 5 to the 4-field hello (rcu -1 never / 0 failed / 1 OK, age in s, -1 never) and to the M line with its field grammar (L/F/S/P, 0/1, dBm | '-' | 'O', [N]dB, lost, 0/1, '?' = unknown), and rename the headings to the ground UNO Q.
verifier_evidence: sketch.ino:1704 sends `H|%s|%d|%d|%ld` = fw | g_rcu_result (-1 never / 0 failed / 1 OK, last rcu_mode() result, :191/:326) | kb | rcu age s. frontpanel.parse_hello (:190-205) maps it through RCU_RESULTS {'1': OK, '0': FAILED, '-1': NEVER} and treats a 3-field hello as 'rcu unknown'. The GDS also sends 'M|sync|tx|rssi|margin|lost|clock' on fp_line (frontpanel.py:24, 166-187). docs/04:891 is headed '9.7 VENTUNO Q: GDS (Linux) <-> station MCU'; its fp_line row lists only S/Q, and fp_in shows '"H|<fw>|<rcu>|<kb>"'. docs/06:192-204 says 'Both run on the VENTUNO Q' and documents 'H|<fw>|<rcu 0/1>|<kb 0/1>' as 'RCU present', with no M line. Neither file changed in 13a60c5..98887f5. A tool written from these docs would send a 3-field hello (RCU stays unknown) and never implement M (matrix blank). Contract section 7 docs phase still pending.
verifier_fix_notes: docs/04 9.7 and docs/06 5: rename to the ground UNO Q. Document the hello as 'H|<fw>|<rcu -1 never/0 failed/1 OK: last rcu_mode result>|<kb 0/1>|<rcu age s, -1 never>' (D-78), and add the M line with its field grammar exactly as in frontpanel.matrix_line() and the sketch's parse_matrix_line(). Add a docs drift test that checks the hello format string and the M field count from sketch.ino.

title: docs/15 still documents the old (VENTUNO) station pin plan and old defaults: RCU AUX D4, lamps D5/D6/D7, buzzer A0, SX NRST A1, archive_max_gb 16, fault_log false
description: The code (sketch.ino:149/152/532, pin plan H, D-72) uses RCU M0/M1/AUX = D2/D3/D7, lamps AOS/ALARM/UPLINK = D4/D5/D6, buzzer A1, SX126x NRST A4. docs/15 contradicts this in: section 5 heading 'Station sketch build settings (VENTUNO Q MCU)' (line 430); line 437 'RCU on D2 M0, D3 M1, D4 AUX'; line 441 'PIN_SX_NRST ... A1'; line 444 'PIN_RCU_AUX D4'; line 445 'D5, D6, D7, A0'; and line 406 ([gds] rcu 'M0/M1/AUX on D2/D3/D4'). It also contradicts config.py: line 410 archive_max_gb default 16.0 (code 8.0, D-80) and line 277 fault_log default 'false' (code: true for model = E22-400T37S, fault_log_default(), D-77). docs/13:2997 also still says 'default 16 GB'. tests/test_docs.py does not check these values.
failure_scenario: An operator wires the station from docs/15. The E22 AUX output goes to D4, which the sketch drives as the AOS lamp output: two outputs fight on one net, the RCU never sees AUX and reports FAILED. The SX126x NRST lands on A1, the buzzer driver, so the radio is reset by every buzzer tone. A T37S user reads that the abnormal-status log is off by default when it is on.
proposed_fix: Update docs/15: section 5 title to the ground UNO Q; the PIN_RCU_* row to D2/D3/D7; the PIN_LED_*/PIN_BUZZER row to D4/D5/D6/A1; PIN_SX_NRST to A4; the [gds] rcu text to D2/D3/D7; archive_max_gb default to 8.0 (D-80); fault_log default to 'model-dependent: true for E22-400T37S, else false'. Fix docs/13:2997 to 8 GB. Add a docs test that reads these rows from sketch.ino and config.DEFAULTS.
verifier_evidence: sketch.ino:149 `PIN_RCU_M0 = 2, PIN_RCU_M1 = 3, PIN_RCU_AUX = 7`; :152 `PIN_LED_AOS = 4, PIN_LED_ALARM = 5, PIN_LED_UPLINK = 6, PIN_BUZZER = A1`; :532 `PIN_SX_NRST = A4`. docs/15 at 98887f5 has: line 430 heading 'Station sketch build settings (VENTUNO Q MCU)'; 437 'RCU on D2 M0, D3 M1, D4 AUX'; 441 PIN_SX_NRST A1; 444 PIN_RCU_AUX D4; 445 'D5, D6, D7, A0'; 406 '[gds] rcu ... M0/M1/AUX on D2/D3/D4'; 410 archive_max_gb 16.0, against config.py:107 8.0 (changed in this diff, D-80); 277 fault_log 'false' with no mention of the model-dependent default (config.py:144-150 fault_log_default, D-77). docs/13:2997 says 'default 16 GB'. The diff edited docs/15 (still_rate_dps rows, key count, --sim row) and left these rows stale. No test reads docs/15 (no test references 15_Configuration_Reference). The problem is wider than reported: docs/03:514/570/603/671 (ground section) also still give RCU AUX on 'VENTUNO Q D4'. So both wiring sources lead to AUX on D4, which the sketch drives as the AOS lamp output, and NRST on A1, the buzzer. Contract section 7 puts the docs overhaul in a later phase, but at this commit the docs contradict the code, with a wiring hazard.
verifier_fix_notes: docs/15: section 5 title -> ground UNO Q MCU; DSSQ_RADIO_SX126X text and PIN_RCU_* -> D2/D3/D7; PIN_LED_*/PIN_BUZZER -> D4/D5/D6/A1; PIN_SX_NRST -> A4 (RXEN/TXEN A2/A3 unchanged); [gds] rcu -> D2/D3/D7; archive_max_gb -> 8.0 (D-80); fault_log -> 'model-dependent: true for model = "E22-400T37S", else false (D-77)'. docs/13:2997 -> 8 GB. Same pin fix in docs/03 ground-station tables and diagrams (lines ~514, 570, 603, 671). Add a docs test that parses the PIN_* constants from sketch.ino and config.DEFAULTS and checks them against the docs/15 rows.

title: Station pin tables in docs still give the old pin plan; wiring by them puts the E22 AUX output against the new AOS lamp output on D4
description: Code (pin plan H, sketch.ino:149-152, 532): RCU M0 D2, M1 D3, AUX D7; lamps AOS D4, ALARM D5, UPLINK D6; buzzer A1; SX126x NRST A4. The docs still give AUX D4, lamps D5/D6/D7, buzzer A0 and NRST A1. Affected lines: docs/15:437, 443, 444, 445 and docs/15:406 ('[gds] rcu ... D2/D3/D4'); docs/06_Displays.md:69-72 and 182; docs/03_Hardware_Integration.md:514-515, 570, 603, 620, 623 and 671-676; docs/00_Beginner_Setup_Guide.md:683, 698, 701 and 887; docs/14_Troubleshooting_and_Event_Response.md:88. In 3.1, setup() drives D4 as a push-pull OUTPUT (the AOS lamp, sketch.ino:1669-1670). The E22 AUX pin is an output that drives high and low (T33D manual 5.6).
failure_scenario: An owner wires the ground E22 by docs/03 5.1 or docs/00 (AUX to D4, UPLINK LED to D7) and flashes 3.1. D4 is held LOW (AOS off) while the idle module drives AUX HIGH, so two outputs fight on one line. D7 (the RCU AUX input, pull-up) reads HIGH with nothing driving it, so every rcu_mode() reports 'OK' while the module is not followed. The lamps sit one pin off and the buzzer on A0 never sounds.
proposed_fix: Update every station pin table and diagram to plan H: AUX D7 (PB2), AOS D4, ALARM D5, UPLINK D6, buzzer A1, SX126x NRST A4 (PC1), A0 free. That covers docs/15 section 5 plus the rcu row, docs/06 section 2 / RCU table, docs/03 5.1 / 5.3.1 / 5.4 / 5.5 mermaid, docs/00 and docs/14:88.
verifier_evidence: Code (plan H, D-72): sketch.ino:149 PIN_RCU_M0 = 2, M1 = 3, AUX = 7; 152 AOS = 4, ALARM = 5, UPLINK = 6, BUZZER = A1; 532 PIN_SX_NRST = A4. The harness asserts the same (test_e22.cpp: 'pin plan H'). setup() 1669-1670 makes D4 an OUTPUT driven LOW. The docs still give the old plan. docs/15:437 and 444 say AUX D4; 443 says NRST A1; 445 says lamps D5/D6/D7 and buzzer A0; 406 says 'D2/D3/D4'. docs/06:69-72 and 182; docs/00:683, 698, 700, 701, 887 and 891 (also 'on the VENTUNO Q, A0 drives the buzzer'); docs/03:514, 570, 603, 622, 623, 671 and 676; docs/14:88. Further stale spots the GS list missed: docs/01:297-298 (lamps D5/D6/D7, buzzer A0, AUX D4) and 352 (NRST A1); docs/03:330, 360 and 365; docs/07:659; README.md:178; docs/FAQ.md:237. The T33D manual 5.6 says AUX outputs a high level when idle and a low level when busy, so a D4 driven LOW against an idle AUX is two outputs fighting. Anyone wiring lamps by these docs gets lamps one pin off (the AOS LED on D5 shows ALARM, the ALARM LED on D6 shows UPLINK, the UPLINK LED on D7 is never driven) and a silent buzzer on A0. One correction to the failure scenario: with the UPLINK LED wired to D7 per the old docs, the AUX input's internal pull-up into that LED + 330 ohm gives an undefined level near the LED's forward voltage, not a guaranteed HIGH. rcu_mode() may report OK or FAILED unpredictably; it is not always 'OK'. The docs phase (contract section 7) is still to come, but at 98887f5 these are the shipped wiring instructions.
verifier_fix_notes: Update every station pin table and diagram to plan H: M0 D2, M1 D3, AUX D7 (PB2); AOS D4, ALARM D5, UPLINK D6; buzzer A1 (PA5); SX126x NRST A4 (PC1); A0 free. That covers docs/15 section 5 (437, 443-445) and the [gds] rcu row (406); docs/06 section 2 and the RCU table; docs/03 (330, 360, 365, 514, 570, 603, 622-623, 671-676); docs/00 (683, 698-701, 887, 891); docs/01 (297-298, 352); docs/07:659; docs/14:88; FAQ:237; README.md:178. Leave the historical test record docs/21:638 and the D-68 entry docs/12:911 as recorded history (label them). Optionally add a docs drift test that greps the station pin constants out of sketch.ino and compares them with docs/15 section 5.

title: docs/15 contradicts the 3.1 configuration defaults (fault_log, archive_max_gb, key count) and leaves out --mode2-confirmed
description: docs/15:277 gives fault_log default 'false'. config.merge() / fault_log_default() (config.py:143-163) now make an absent fault_log true for model = "E22-400T37S", and station.toml no longer contains the key. docs/15:410 gives archive_max_gb 16.0; config.py:107 and station.toml now use 8.0 (D-80). docs/15:424 says '92 in the shipped file'; the shipped file now holds 91 keys (82 + 8 radio.sx126x before; fault_log removed, still_rate_dps and still_vib_mg added), and fault_log is now an optional key outside the file. The new configuration-tool option --mode2-confirmed (radio/e22.py:439) is not documented anywhere. docs/00:649, docs/03:587 and docs/16:507 still show the tool command without it.
failure_scenario: An operator configuring a T37S reads docs/15, believes the abnormal-status log is off unless set, and writes 'fault_log = false', or expects no FF FF FF 0x reports. An operator sizing the archive believes the cap is 16 GB on a 32 GB eMMC. A scripted (non-TTY) run of the documented e22 command now exits 'not confirmed: nothing sent' with no documented way past it.
proposed_fix: docs/15:277: default 'absent: true for model = "E22-400T37S", false otherwise (D-77)'. docs/15:410: 8.0 (D-80). docs/15:424: '91 in the shipped file plus the optional field_ut, min_rate and fault_log'. Add --mode2-confirmed to docs/15 section 6 and to the e22 command lines in docs/00, 03, 14 and 16.
verifier_evidence: docs/15:277 gives fault_log default 'false'. config.merge() (config.py:143-145) applies fault_log_default(), which returns True for model = "E22-400T37S" when the key is absent. The shipped station.toml no longer sets it. docs/15:410 gives archive_max_gb 16.0; config.py:107 has 8.0 (D-80). The same stale 16 GB also appears at docs/07:683, docs/18:277, docs/20:203 (L-42) and dssq-groundstation/README.md:124. Key count, measured with tomllib (verify-GS/countkeys.py): the shipped file held 90 keys at 13a60c5 and holds 91 at 98887f5. fault_log was removed; still_rate_dps and still_vib_mg were added. The diff changed docs/15:424 from '90 in the shipped file' to '92', counting the +2 but not the -1. --mode2-confirmed exists only in radio/e22.py:439 and tests/test_radio.py; grep finds it in no doc. The documented commands (docs/00:649, docs/03:587, docs/15:35, docs/16:507) still work interactively: on a TTY confirm_mode2() prompts for 'mode2'. Without a TTY the tool exits 'not confirmed: nothing sent' (e22.py:452-454).
verifier_fix_notes: docs/15:277: default 'absent = true for model = "E22-400T37S", false otherwise (D-77); set false only to switch the T37S log off'. docs/15:410 and the copies in docs/07, 18, 20 and README: 8.0 (D-80). docs/15:424: '93 keys (91 in the shipped file plus the optional [science] field_ut, [linkmgr] min_rate and [radio] fault_log)'. Add --mode2-confirmed and the interactive 'mode2' prompt to docs/15 section 6 and to the e22 tool command lines in docs/00, 03, 15:35 and 16. A docs drift test comparing the docs/15 default column with config.DEFAULTS would catch this class of drift.

title: The sigma multiples given for still_rate_dps / still_vib_mg are wrong
description: docs/15:366-367 call the thresholds about 3 sigma (rate) and about 3.5 sigma (vibration) of the three-axis datasheet noise, and docs/13:2702 says 'about 3 sigma'. With the same docs' noise values (0.07 deg/s and 1.2 mg per axis, i.e. 0.121 deg/s and 2.08 mg over three axes), 0.5 deg/s is 4.1 sigma and 10 mg is 4.8 sigma. The 3 sigma / 3.5 sigma values would be 0.36 deg/s and 7.3 mg (R3 section 5.9).
failure_scenario: An operator tuning the thresholds from the docs sets still_rate_dps = 0.36 ('3 sigma'). The peak of 200 or more samples of a 3-D Gaussian magnitude at rest reaches about 3.6-4.2 sigma, so a body at rest is flagged as moving.
proposed_fix: Write "about 4 sigma (0.5 / 0.121)" and "about 5 sigma (10 / 2.08)", and note that a peak over many samples needs that margin.
verifier_evidence: docs/15:366-367 say still_rate_dps 0.5 is 'about 3 sigma of the three-axis gyro noise (0.07 deg/s per axis)' and still_vib_mg 10 'about 3.5 sigma' of 1.2 mg per axis. docs/13:2702 says 'about 3 sigma'. With the three-axis values the same docs use (0.121 deg/s, 2.08 mg), 0.5 is 4.12 sigma and 10 is 4.81 sigma (computed). R3 section 5.9 derived 3 sigma = 0.36 deg/s and 3.5 sigma = 7 mg and then chose 0.5 and 10, so the docs copied the sigma words but not the chosen values. The finding's failure scenario is overstated. Simulation of the peak of a 3-D Gaussian magnitude: for 200 samples the median is 2.13 and the 95th percentile 2.51 three-axis sigma (3.7 / 4.3 per-axis sigma); P(peak > 0.36 deg/s) is about 0.05 % for 200 samples and 1 % for 2000. So a 0.36 threshold would rarely flag a body at rest under datasheet white noise. The doc contradiction is real; the claimed consequence is not.
verifier_fix_notes: Correct the text in docs/15 and docs/13 9.4: 'about 4 sigma (0.5 / 0.121)' and 'about 5 sigma (10 / 2.08) of the three-axis datasheet noise, margin for the peak over many samples and the unspecified 25 Hz noise, VERIFY T-SC-14'. No code change.
